title: AufZack-S: Everyday life and fitness - Activating physical activity program for seniors to cope with everyday life - Effectiveness
summary:
Background:
As people age, it often becomes more difficult for them to stay physically fit and manage their daily lives independently. This decline is usually even more pronounced when they become dependent on care. At the same time, there is a strong emphasis on enabling older adults to live at home or in assisted living settings for as long as possible. However, there are currently very few suitable exercise programs in these settings, even though many residents are insufficiently physically active. Due to demographic changes and a shortage of care professionals, there is a growing need for simple measures that help maintain older adults’ independence.

Method:
The “AufZack-S” project is testing a practical, everyday exercise program. It consists of short activity sessions (“movement snacks”) that combine physical and cognitive exercises. These are intended to be carried out independently several times per week, supported by special dice that suggest the exercises. The effectiveness of this program is being evaluated in a study by comparing a participating group with a control group.

Research Question:
The aim is to determine whether these short activity sessions can improve physical and cognitive performance, enhance well-being, maintain independence in daily life, and reduce the need for care.
